title: Minimax Regret for Quantile-Optimal Policy Thresholds at a Vanishing-Information Boundary
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered incremental below field floor: paper_score_ceiling 6 < 7.4; narrow known-nuisance triangular class and no executed full-class certified interval.
gap_reasons: The note proves an exact asymptotic minimax characterization only for a highly constructed triangular location model with known density, propensity, slope, localization scale, and a shape class tailored to the threshold rearrangement.

The finite-program theorem supplies symbolic convergent error bounds, but no outward-rounded program has been executed, the stated two-root validation has not been performed, and no usable full-class value interval is delivered.

Position the claimed all-policy weak-overlap minimax frontier against accepted-bank stat_policy_regret_margin_overlap_v1, stating at theorem level why its margin/mean-welfare rate frontier neither proves nor subsumes this marginal-quantile Gaussian-value result.
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation built an analytic local Gaussian minimax characterization and a convergent symbolic finite program; the dedicated math referee passed. The field-floor review graded the delivered note incremental because its known-nuisance triangular class is narrow and no usable outward-rounded full-class interval was computed. Under the current cover bound, a nonvacuous certificate already needs r > 912 before other errors, so a practical computation requires a new scalable method and a justified calibration. The decision panel also requested a comparison with the accepted mean-welfare rate result; that positioning edit remains open.
tldr: For the explicitly defined triangular known-nuisance class, a lower-quartile policy threshold approaches a boundary where treatment information vanishes. The note derives the policy-quantile loss, proves two-direction Le Cam convergence to weighted Gaussian white noise, and identifies a positive sharp \(n^{1/2}\) minimax regret constant against every measurable randomized assignment policy. The all-policy reduction uses an explicit low-, matched-, and high-mass clamp. A bounded observable score vector converges in total variation to the normalized Gaussian coordinates, yielding an asymptotically attaining data-only rule. Explicit Bernstein cells, deterministic representatives, Gaussian projection, observation quantization, and action discretization define finite programs with analytic endpoints \(V_r^-\leq V\leq V_r^+\) and \(V_r^+-V_r^-\to0\). No finite outward-rounded nonvacuous bracket has yet been computed; that numerical implementation is the open-ended question.
gap: Wang, Zhou, Song, and Sherwood derive nonstandard asymptotics for an estimated marginal-quantile policy under conventional overlap, while Hirano and Porter derive Gaussian limit-experiment treatment rules for smooth welfare contrasts. Neither result supplies the boundary-weighted experiment, the marginal-mixture quartile loss, or the full compact-class minimax value when \(e(x)\) vanishes at the optimizing threshold. Existing finite quantile-regret games and finite epsilon-minimax algorithms also do not close this infinite parameter, observation, and action approximation problem.
fill: The theorem package proves equivalence in both deficiency directions, a uniform CDF inversion, an explicit three-case all-policy rearrangement converse, positivity through an analytic two-root game, total-variation transfer from bounded observable scores to normalized Gaussian coordinates, data-only attainment, and convergent finite certificates based on explicit Bernstein cells and deterministic representatives. The open-ended component asks for a reproducible interval-arithmetic implementation whose first finite certificate is informative in the solved two-root benchmark and then for the full class.
